# CTR Decompilation — Function Tracking

Tracks per-function decompilation progress in the Ghidra project. See `CLAUDE.md` for the
definition of `Decompiled` and the verification rules.

## Build / target

- Ghidra program: `SCUS_944.26.exe` (PSX:LE:32, image base `0x80000000`), **NTSC-U**.
- This is the **926** build. Confirmed by matching unique addresses against the decomp
  symbol maps: `BOTS_Driver_Init = 0x80017164` matches `symbols/syms926.txt` /
  `symbols/gcc-syms926.txt` exactly.
- **Reference symbol map (candidates only, must verify):** `src/decompile/symbols/syms926.txt`.
  Addresses in this map line up 1:1 with the Ghidra DB; `FUN_xxxxxxxx` names there give
  candidate names to validate against actual behavior — never apply blindly.
- Scope: NTSC-U (926) only. Ignore the 603/805/903/1006/1020/1111 builds.
- Reminder (per CLAUDE.md + user): trust nothing. Existing non-`FUN_` names in the Ghidra DB
  (CTR-tools community attempt) are also unverified hints and must be checked when touched.

## Status legend

- `Untouched` — default Ghidra/auto-generated state, not yet analyzed.
- `In progress` — under active analysis; see Status note for blockers.
- `Decompiled` — meets every bar in `CLAUDE.md` (all globals/calls/locals named & typed,
  top comment present, layout accurate).

### Batch 89 (2026-06-29) — OVR_233 cutscene script-opcode reader cluster (6 funcs, verified)

The b88 "decoder cluster" turned out to be the cutscene **script-command (opcode) reader** for `struct CutsceneObj`
(NOT an anim/keyframe decoder — corrected). All 6 verified line-for-line vs decomp
`src/decompile/WorkInProgress/src/233/233_02_09_CS_ScriptCmd.c` and renamed + prototyped + plated + **saved**:

- **CS_ScriptCmd_ReadOpcode_Main@OVR_233::800ac014** (was FUN_…800ac014) — decodes one cutscene-script command from
  the byte stream `cs->currOpcode`(+0x38) into the `cs->metadata`(+0x10, short[]) record. Reads the opcode byte, looks
  up a field-presence bitmask in global table `0x800b14cc` (&DAT_OVR_233__800b14cc), then conditionally pulls fields:
  bits 0x1/0x2/0x4→metadata[1..3]=GetShort, 0x8→metadata[4]=GetInt (XA Category), 0x10→metadata[6]=GetInt (XA Index),
  0x20→align-4 + metadata[6]=GetInt_dup (Oxide-intro path), 0x40/0x80→metadata[8..9]=GetShort. Sets cs->prevOpcode(+0x40)
  to the end-of-command cursor; leading `currOpcode!=prevOpcode` guard skips re-decode.
- **CS_ScriptCmd_OpcodeAt@OVR_233::800ac1ec** — seek script to explicit ptr (currOpcode=opCodeAt, prevOpcode=-1, decode).
- **CS_ScriptCmd_OpcodeNext@OVR_233::800ac1c0** — advance to next command (currOpcode = saved end cursor, prevOpcode=-1, decode).
- **CS_ScriptCmd_ReadOpcode_GetShort@OVR_233::800abf70** — read s16 from cursor, advance 2 (returns sign-extended int).
- **CS_ScriptCmd_ReadOpcode_GetInt@OVR_233::800abf9c** — read little-endian u32 from cursor, advance 4.
- **CS_ScriptCmd_ReadOpcode_GetInt_dup@OVR_233::800abfd8** — byte-identical twin of GetInt (decomp notes "same as above").

CutsceneObj fields VERIFIED (documented in plates; struct not yet created in DB → `cs` typed `int`, TODO build
`struct CutsceneObj` then retype): metadata@0x10 (short*), currOpcode@0x38 (char*), prevOpcode@0x40 (char*, 0xffffffff=none).

### Batch 206 (2026-06-30) — OVR_226 investigated + documented (the "Renderer" overlay) — STOP point reached

it is **HAND-WRITTEN ASSEMBLY** with a custom **register-passing calling convention** — no standard prologues,
args arrive in registers ($at = render context, $s3-$s6 = a quad's 4 screen-coord vertex records, $t9 = work pool,

+0x184 draw), and some **instructions overlap** (branch-into-middle). Ghidra cannot recover these to C; this is the
classic **register-passing GTE dead-end** category (per CLAUDE.md: no speculative names — documented, not forced).

  plate (+0x28/2c clip bounds, +0x70 visible-subtri flags, +0x148 subdivide table, +0x184 draw table, +0x194 sign
  mask, +0x1a0/1ac UVs, +0x324 recursion limit, +0x3d8 tex-anim UVs, +0xb4 scratch midpoint, …).
- **OVR226_Render_InterpEdgeMidpoint@OVR_226::800a1408** — named (verified: averages an edge's 2 endpoint XYZ +

### Batch 248 (2026-06-30) — libcd CD driver: created + applied CdlIntr/CdlCommand enums (magic status/command bytes → named)

Continued the b247 data-driven hunt → the remaining high-xref untyped globals are the libcd CD-driver status/command bytes. Found the KEY:
CD_ready's timeout printf indexes debug string tables by these very bytes — `(&PTR_s_NoIntr_8008c4c0)[g_nCdSyncStatus]` and
`(&PTR_s_CdlSync_8008c440)[g_bCdLastCommand]` — so the binary itself names every value.
- Read the intr-name table @0x8008c4c0 → strings @0x8001224c.. = `DiskError/DataEnd/Acknowledge/Complete/DataReady/NoIntr` (indices 5..0).
  **Created `enum CdlIntr` (1 byte): CdlNoIntr=0/CdlDataReady=1/CdlComplete=2/CdlAcknowledge=3/CdlDataEnd=4/CdlDiskError=5** (verified, matches standard PSYQ libcd).
- Applied CdlIntr to **g_eCdSyncStatus@8008c6f8** + **g_eCdReadyStatus@8008c6f9**; applied the pre-existing **CdlCommand** enum to **g_eCdLastCommand@8008c439**.
- Verified: CdInterruptHandler now reads `g_eCdSyncStatus = CdlComplete/CdlAcknowledge/CdlDiskError`, `g_eCdReadyStatus = CdlDataReady/CdlDataEnd`
  (were magic 1/2/3/4/5); CD_ready shows `if (g_eCdReadyStatus != CdlNoIntr)`. Cleans the whole CD driver (~11 fns: CD_cw/ready/sync/datasync/
  CdInterruptHandler/CdLastCom). The CdInterruptHandler plate already documented "1=DataReady..5=DiskError" — enum matches exactly.

**REUSABLE TECHNIQUE — applying an enum to a global whose name has a mismatched Hungarian prefix:** apply_data_type + set_global both HARD-REJECT
(apply_data_type wants an `e` prefix for enums but set_global/rename_data only accept dw/n/p/sz/ab/pfn — a linter catch-22). WORKAROUND that works:
`create_label(addr, "g_e<Name>")` (create_label bypasses the Hungarian check) → `delete_label(addr, "<old g_n/g_b name>")` (so g_e is primary) →
`apply_data_type(addr, "<Enum>")` (now the `e` prefix matches). Renames g_nCdSyncStatus→g_eCdSyncStatus etc. as a side effect (accurate: they're enums now). **Saved.**

name_substring=MenuState include_all_sections=true`. VERIFIED all 8 write sites use only 0-5 (no out-of-range sentinel → safe per the b256
enum-on-field lesson): LOAD_TenStages=4(garage), MainFreeze_MenuPtrDefault=1/2/3, MainFreeze_HandleSelection=0(quit), UI_RaceEnd_MenuProc=0/1/2/3,
MM_Title_MenuUpdate=4/5, MM_Scrapbook_PlayMovie=0, CS_Garage_MenuProc=0, CS_Credits_End=5, CS_Camera_ThTick_Podium=0. The LOAD_TenStages
DRIVER_MODELS-stage dispatch now reads `switch(sdata_mainMenuState){case MM_TITLE:MM_JumpTo_Title_FirstTime;...case MM_GARAGE:CS_Garage_Init;
case MM_SCRAPBOOK:MM_JumpTo_Scrapbook;}` and writes `= MM_GARAGE`. Names/semantics match b66 design exactly.

LESSON (important): `audit_globals_in_function` omitting a global does NOT mean it's synthetic/unaddressable — it only lists UNNAMED ones. Use

CORRECTS the old memory note that OVR "can't be addressed" — it CAN, with the overlay-qualified entry.
